Birth-month and school-entry-age instrumental variable illustration

Source: R/package_documentation.R
birth_school_age.Rd

A reconstructed individual-level dataset used to illustrate testing the monotonicity of an instrument. This is NOT a set of real individual records: it is generated to match the aggregate proportions reported in Black et al. (2011), Table 1 (cross-tabulating month of birth and school-entry timing) and Table 3 (the "discontinuity subsample" of 104,023 subjects born in January or December, rounded here to 104,000 and split evenly between the two birth months, following Fiorini and Stevens (2014)).

Subjects born in December tend to enter school on-time or late, while subjects born in January tend to enter early or on-time, making month of birth a natural candidate instrument for school-entry age – see demo_code/RIllustration20221028.Rmd for the full worked example (testing the bounded null and estimating the range of individual effects of birth month on school-entry age).

Usage

birth_school_age

Format

A data frame with 104,000 rows and 3 variables:

BirthMonth

character - "Dec" or "Jan".

EntryTiming

character - "Early", "On-Time", or "Late".

EntryAge

double - school-entry age, in years, implied by BirthMonth and EntryTiming.
